title: Fomo Kernel trigger-matrix prompt corpus (#458)
description: One locale/split slice of the trigger corpus: evals/triggers/corpus/<locale>/<split>.json. The readable contract; evals/triggers/run_triggers.py's load_corpus()/load_corpus_file() hold the enforcement, because the offline suite carries no jsonschema dependency (same posture as evals/episodes/episode.schema.json).

locale.description: Must match the file's own parent directory name. Locale is the corpus dimension; host is an execution dimension carried only in the result log (see the module docstring in run_triggers.py for why the corpus is not also split per host).

split.description: Must match the file's own filename. calibration may inform one bounded trigger-description iteration (#458); holdout is the untouched release-decision evidence and must never be read, quoted, or reasoned about while writing or adjusting a trigger description.

prompts.description: Exactly 20 items per class (review_positive, pre_trade_positive, adjacent_negative) -- enforced by load_corpus_file(), not merely documented here.

id.description: Stable id, unique across the entire corpus (every locale and split), not merely within one file -- load_corpus() checks this globally so a copy-paste across a locale or split boundary cannot slip in unnoticed.

class.description: review_positive: the user is asking for a retrospective review of trades already made. pre_trade_positive: the user is weighing a trade not yet made, against their own book -- M1's capability. adjacent_negative: market/research/education/general-advice content that must NOT trigger the skill; the corpus's hard cases sit deliberately near the boundary of one of the two positive classes rather than being obviously off-topic.

text.description: The literal opening message text, in the prompt's own locale script and vocabulary. Never machine-translated from another locale's prompt (docs/language-policy.md; the module docstring explains why zh-TW and zh-CN are authored independently).

note.description: English maintainer-facing design rationale: what variation this prompt exercises, or (for adjacent_negative) what makes it a near-miss rather than an obviously off-topic prompt. Never shown to a host or a user -- data for whoever reads the bank, the same role episode.schema.json's answers[].note plays.

near_miss_of.description: Required on adjacent_negative prompts only (forbidden on the two positive classes). Which boundary this prompt sits near: a positive class's trigger surface, or general market/research/education content not closer to either ("general"). Used for the corpus's own boundary-coverage check (tests/test_triggers.py) -- every locale/split must exercise all three values, not only obviously-negative content.
